'''Todorokihimenomikoto Shrine''' (止止呂支比売命神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|Sumiyoshi-ku]], [[:en:Osaka City|Osaka City]], {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}. It is classified as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor shrine) and was formerly designated as a [[village shrine]] under the old shrine Ranking system.

== Enshrined Deities ==
* [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]] 
* [[Kushinadahime|Inadahime-no-Mikoto]]

== History ==
The founding date of the shrine is unknown. The name "Todoroki" is believed to derive from the name of a bridge that once existed within the precincts. Another theory suggests that the name originates from calling [[Kushinadahime|Inadahime-no-Mikoto]] "Todorokihime." Some also attribute the name to the sound of a stream flowing through the precincts, with "todoroki" (thundering or roaring) evolving into its current form.<ref name="Osaka Health Association">[https://osaka-hk.org/posts/senjin125 Historical Overview of Todorokihimenomikoto Shrine - Osaka Health Association] Retrieved March 19, 2019</ref> Listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō}} as a minor shrine, it is thought to have originally served as an auxiliary shrine (okunoin) to the {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|Sumiyoshi-taisha|qid=Q705949|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha}}.

In 1220 (Shōkyū 2), during Emperor Go-Toba's pilgrimage to {{ill|Kumano shrine|lt=Kumano shrine|lt=Kumano Shrine|ja|熊野三山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shrine|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the chief priest of Sumiyoshi Taisha, Tsutsumori Tsunekuni, constructed a temporary palace (angū) in a pine grove on the shrine grounds. Known as the "Wakamatsu Gosho" (Young Pine Palace), the shrine subsequently came to be called "Wakamatsu Shrine." <ref name="Osaka City">[http://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/kensetsu/page/0000009370.html Todorokihimenomikoto Shrine - Osaka City] Retrieved March 19, 2019</ref>

== Shrine Grounds ==
{{right|[[File:若松行宮祉.JPG|thumb|none|Wakamatsu Temporary Palace Site]]}}
* Monument marking the site of the Wakamatsu Temporary Palace.
* Stone marker for Tensuifun Toyoura no Mikoto Shrine (Osaka City-designated cultural property).

=== Auxiliary Shrines ===
* '''Tensuifun Toyoura no Mikoto Shrine''': Enshrines {{ill|Kōjin|en|Kōjin|qid=Q6455190|lt=Sambaō Gongen}} ({{ill|Mikumari|lt=Mikumari|lt=Mikumari-no-Kami|ja|水分神|2=ja|3=水分神|4=zh|5=水分神|6=sv|7=Mikumari-no-Kami|8=fr|9=Mikumari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikumari-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Okitsu-hiko-no-Mikoto|ja|奥津彦命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okitsu-hiko-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=DELETED_QID|dd=Q135550732}}, {{ill|Okitsu-hime-no-Mikoto|ja|奥津姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okitsu-hime-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=DELETED_QID|dd=Q135550733}}), [[Ōkuninushi]], and [[Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|Kotoshironushi]]. This shrine, also known as Aramatsubara Arajinja, was originally located in Andatsu 2-chome, {{ill|Suminoe-ku, Osaka|en|Suminoe-ku, Osaka|qid=Q985711|lt=Suminoe-ku}}, before being relocated to Todorokihimenomikoto Shrine in 1907 (Meiji 40). It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} with no former Rank.

'''Todorokihimenomikoto Shrine''' (止止呂支比売命神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|en|Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|qid=Q985702|lt=Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka|en|Osaka|qid=Q35765|lt=Osaka City}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}, Japan. It is listed as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and was formerly Ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

* {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inadahime-no-Mikoto|qid=Q505469|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q505469}}

== History ==
The exact date of establishment is unknown. The name "Todoroki" is believed to originate from a bridge that once existed within the shrine grounds. Another theory suggests it comes from referring to Inadahime as "Todorokihime" or from the sound of a babbling brook that once flowed through the grounds, with "Todoroki" meaning "roaring" or "resounding."

Originally, it served as an auxiliary shrine (inner sanctuary) of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|Sumiyoshi-taisha|qid=Q705949|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha}}. During {{ill|Emperor Go-Toba|en|Emperor Go-Toba|qid=Q316658|lt=Emperor Go-Toba}}'s pilgrimage to {{ill|Kumano region|en|Kumano region|qid=Q6443450|lt=Kumano}} in {{ill|1220|en|1220|qid=Q5392|lt=1220}} ({{ill|Jōkyū|en|Jōkyū|qid=Q1195428|lt=Shōkū era}} 2), a temporary palace called "Wakamatsu Palace" was erected in the shrine’s pine forest by {{ill|Tsumori Tsunekuni|ja|津守経国|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori Tsunekuni|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to the shrine also being referred to as '''Wakamatsu Palace''' or '''Wakamatsu Shrine'''.

== Precincts ==
* Monument of the Wakamatsu Palace Site
* Stone Marker of {{ill|Amemiketsutoyora-no-Mikoto Shrine|ja|天水分豊浦命社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amemiketsutoyora-no-Mikoto Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Designated Cultural Property of Osaka City)

== Auxiliary Shrines ==
* {{ill|Amemiketsutoyora-no-Mikoto Shrine|ja|天水分豊浦命神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amemiketsutoyora-no-Mikoto Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Deities: {{ill|Sanbo Kojin|ja|三宝荒神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanbō Kōjīn|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q13577821}} ({{ill|Mikumari|lt=Mikumari|lt=Mikumari-no-Kami|ja|水分神|2=ja|3=水分神|4=zh|5=水分神|6=sv|7=Mikumari-no-Kami|8=fr|9=Mikumari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikumari-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Okutsuhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|奥津彦命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okutsuhiko-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=DELETED_QID|dd=Q135550732}}, {{ill|Okutsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|奥津姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okutsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=DELETED_QID|dd=Q135550733}}), {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}})

It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and was formerly an {{ill|Unranked shrines|ja|無格社|lt=Hokora|qid=Q134917285}}{{efn|Hokora|lt=Unranked Shrine|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917285|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. Also known as Aramatsubara Kōjīn Shrine, it was originally located in {{ill|Anryū|ja|安立|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andachi, Suminoe-ku, Osaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11451168}}, {{ill|Suminoe-ku, Osaka|en|Suminoe-ku, Osaka|qid=Q985711|lt=Suminoe-ku}}, but was merged into Todorokihimenomikoto Shrine in {{ill|1907|en|1907|qid=Q2048|lt=1907}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 40).
